headline: Learned sequence models now target RNA tertiary structure and multi-molecule binding
label: Sequence Models For Biomolecule Design
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair sequence language models with explicit design objectives across RNA, mRNA, and peptide targets.
synthesis: The common thread is pairing learned sequence representations with an explicit design or prediction objective. BeeRNA couples Artificial Bee Colony search with RhoFold-based RMSD scoring to design sequences folding into tertiary RNA structures. RNA-X uses masked language modeling for conditional design against proteins, RNA, and DNA, including multi-target settings. DeepPNI is predictive, using an edge-aware RGCN with ESM-2 features to regress mutation-induced binding free energy changes in protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes. mRNABERT and codonGPT extend this to mRNA design via dual tokenization with protein-contrastive learning and reinforcement learning on a generative language model, respectively. ClsDiff-AMP30 applies classifier-guided diffusion to peptides under 30 residues, with wet-lab validation of 11 selected candidates. New elements are tertiary-structure inverse folding assessed by RMSD and multi-target conditional design spanning molecule types.
